//: Connection settings for orga-login. This file ships WITHOUT the values that
identify a deployment, so that the tool can be distributed publicly.
Nothing here is a credential, and nothing that was removed was one either: the
Cognito app client is PUBLIC (generate_secret = false, PKCE), and every value
removed appears in the user's own address bar on each sign-in. They were taken
out so that a public copy of this tool does not publish the account id, the
pool or the hostname to indexers and scrapers - not because knowing them
grants anything.
The only secret in the whole flow is the user's own refresh token, which
orga-login stores under ~/.orga-ai with 0600 permissions - never here.
THREE LAYERS, lowest precedence first:
1. this file, shipped next to the script
2. ~/.orga-ai/config.json          <- where the deployment values go
3. ORGA_* environment variables
Layer 2 is the one to use, and layer 3 is NOT a substitute for it: Claude Code
runs `orga-login token` through its apiKeyHelper from a non-interactive shell,
which does not reliably inherit variables exported in a terminal. Configure by
file and sign-in works everywhere; configure by environment and sign-in works
while Claude Code fails intermittently.
Layer 2 lives OUTSIDE the repository, so it cannot be committed by accident.
See config.example.json for the shape, and ask your administrator for the
values for your deployment.
Operators: refresh the values from the deployment's Terraform output after any
change to the user pool or its app clients.
//identity_provider: Sends the user straight to one provider, skipping the chooser. Must match the name of a provider registered in the user pool. Kept here rather than moved to layer 2 because it names a product, not a deployment: it identifies neither the client nor the account. Override with ORGA_IDP to use a different provider, or ORGA_IDP="" to reach the local sign-in form.
//redirect_uri: Loopback address this tool listens on while the browser completes the sign-in. Must match a callback URL on the Cognito app client exactly, so the port here and there must agree. Not deployment-identifying, hence kept here.
//claude_models: Written into Claude Code's env by `orga-login setup`. Model names, not secrets.
Why this exists: Claude Code uses whatever model its own release defaults to,
and it updates itself. The gateway only serves the ids in its MODEL_MAP, and
when asked for one it does not know it SUBSTITUTES its default rather than
refusing - so the call succeeds against a different model, and if the two
disagree about the request format the error mentions a 'system' role instead of
the model. Pinning here is what makes a fresh install work first time.
Operators: keep this in step with the model map the gateway serves, and with
which models the account can actually invoke. Set to {} to leave Claude Code
